flashcard_questions.q: Which book about witchcraft did King James I write in 1597?
When did Shakespeare probably write Macbeth?
Which 1604 law made invoking evil spirits a capital offence?
Which animal familiar is named Graymalkin in Act 1, Scene 1?
What is a familiar in Jacobean witchcraft belief?
flashcard_questions.a: An animal companion believed to be given to a witch by the Devil.

flashcard_questions.q: Which paradox do the witches chant that becomes the play’s central motif?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Fair is foul, and foul is fair.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which metre do the witches speak in instead of iambic pentameter?
What is the divine right of kings?
flashcard_questions.a: The belief that a monarch is chosen by God, so killing a king sins against God.

flashcard_questions.q: Which hierarchy places God, angels, the king, nobles, commoners and animals in order?
Which image in Act 2, Scene 4 shows the sun blotted out after the murder?
What happens to Duncan’s horses after his murder, showing nature in revolt?
flashcard_questions.a: They turn wild in nature and eat each other.

flashcard_questions.q: Which bird kills a falcon after Duncan’s murder, inverting the natural order?
Which 1605 plot against Parliament made regicide a topical subject?
Which Catholic priest is the Porter’s ‘equivocator’ thought to refer to?
Which line shows Macbeth knows his face must conceal his intentions?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘False face must hide what the false heart doth know.’

notes: 15 cards: 8 context-to-relevance (Daemonologie, 1606, Witchcraft Act, Gunpowder Plot, Garnet, divine right, Great Chain, Graymalkin), 3 quotation-recall (the paradox, ‘travelling lamp’, ‘False face’), 1 form/metre card (trochaic tetrameter), 1 term-to-definition (familiar), 2 evidence-of-theme (the horses, the owl and falcon). ‘Jacobean’, ‘rhyming couplets’ and ‘fate versus free will’ dropped as glossary flavour or too broad to self-grade. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
